opportunities.title: FY 27 IMMIGRANT LEGAL SERVICES
opportunities.summary: The Department of Youth and Community Development is seeking, via a negotiated acquisition, a contract to provide legal services to non‑citizens—including immigrants, immigrant youth, survivors of domestic violence or trafficking, and immigrant workers—for citizenship, permanent residence and related immigration matters. The award will be issued to Northern Manhattan Improvement Corporation for $374,180 under FY 27, and the notice lists no specific certifications or eligibility requirements.

opportunities.title: FY27 Renewal - FJC Immigration Legal Services
opportunities.agency: Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration
opportunities.summary: The Department of Social Services/Human Resources Administration is renewing its FY27 contract for FJC Immigration Legal Services. The renewal will provide client services under a renewal selection method.

opportunities.title: FY27 Renewal - FJC Immigration Legal Center
opportunities.agency: Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration
opportunities.vendor: New York Legal Assistance Group Inc.
opportunities.summary: The Department of Social Services and the Mayor’s Office to End Domestic and Gender‑Based Violence are renewing a contract to deliver core civil immigration‑related legal services—including status applications, agency and court representation, legal screening, advice, and support for self‑represented clients—at the five New York City Family Justice Centers for survivors of domestic and gender‑based violence.

opportunities.title: FY27 Renewal - FJC Family Law Legal Services
opportunities.agency: Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration
opportunities.summary: The Department of Social Services’ Office of Civil Justice and the Mayor’s Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence are renewing a contract to provide core civil legal services at the city’s five Family Justice Centers. The services include family law assistance—divorce, custody, visitation, and support matters—through screening, advice, pro se assistance, and court representation for survivors of domestic and gender‑based violence.

opportunities.title: The Arches program, which targets high-crime neighborhoods. Procurement is for human client services, as such Competitive Sealed Proposals is the most appropriate source selection method. E jy17 ARCHE
opportunities.summary: The agency is procuring human client services for the Arches program in high‑crime neighborhoods (awarded to Youth Justice Network) and permanent supportive congregate housing and related services for HIV/AIDS clients with mental health or substance‑use needs (awarded to Harlem United Community AIDS Center), as well as Family Justice Center immigration legal services (awarded to Sanctuary for). All contracts are being awarded under Competitive Sealed Proposals.

opportunities.title: In-Person/VRI interpretation for Spoken Languages Services
opportunities.summary: The Administration for Children’s Services (ACS) is awarding three contracts for in‑person and video remote interpretation, deaf/hard‑of‑hearing interpretation, language services, and written translation. These services will support limited‑English proficient and deaf/hard‑of‑hearing families accessing ACS services. The contracts will run from July 1 2026 through June 30 2029 under a competitive sealed proposals selection method.

opportunities.title: Deaf/Hard-of-Hearing Language Access Services
opportunities.summary: The NYC Administration for Children’s Services (ACS) ISLA division is procuring a vendor to deliver sign language interpretation services—including in‑person, on‑site, and video remote interpretation for ASL, Certified Deaf Interpretation, foreign sign languages, and CART—through a competitive sealed proposal. The services will support ACS and its provider network in meeting legal accessibility requirements for limited‑English‑proficient and deaf/hard‑of‑hearing families, with contracts running from July 1 2026 to June 30 2029.

opportunities.title: Translation Services
opportunities.summary: The NYC Administration for Children’s Services (ACS) is procuring vendors to provide in‑person and video‑remote interpretation for spoken languages, deaf/hard‑of‑hearing interpretation, and written translation services. The services will support ACS and its provider network in meeting language access requirements for limited‑English‑proficient and deaf/hard‑of‑hearing families. Contracts will run from July 1 2026 through June 30 2029.

opportunities.title: LEGAL SERVICES FOR IMMIGRANTS WORKERS
opportunities.summary: The City is purchasing legal services to assist non‑citizens—including immigrants, immigrant youth, survivors of domestic violence and trafficking, and immigrant workers—with applications for citizenship, permanent residence and related matters. The services will be provided to the Department of Youth and Community Development under a negotiated acquisition contract (Other) awarded to Make the Road New York.

opportunities.title: LEGAL SERVICES FOR IMMIGRANTS WORKERS
opportunities.agency: Compass Center Base Cd - Bronx 04 Middle -
opportunities.summary: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded a negotiated acquisition contract (PIN 26026N0021001) to Make the Road New York to provide legal services to non‑citizens, including immigrants, immigrant youth, survivors of domestic violence and trafficking, and immigrant workers. The contract is valued at $412,153 and will be administered under the negotiated acquisition vehicle.

opportunities.title: FY27 Renewal - NYCitizenship Program
opportunities.agency: Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration
opportunities.vendor: New York Legal Assistance Group Inc.
opportunities.summary: The Department of Social Services/Human Resources Administration is renewing a FY27 contract to provide legal screenings and services to participants in the NYCitizenship Program. The contract includes free legal assistance that guides clients through the naturalization process to help them become eligible for SSI and reduce reliance on DSS benefits.
